failed_joints.SHOULDER_LIFT: SHOULDER_LIFT: unresponsive (actuator appears failed-open). The observer saw none of 6 of 6 reliability-burst moves -- an oscillation between two positions this joint had already been watched to reach, so those moves were known-real and should have been plainly visible. Across the whole burst the pack stayed flat (7.30V -> 7.56V, delta -0.259V, within the 0.02V measurement noise floor) and the transport reported no stall time. No motion, no current drawn and nothing pushed against: that is the signature of a disconnected / failed-open servo, not of a camera that cannot see. A jammed-but-live servo would have drawn locked-rotor current and sagged the pack, or accrued stall time pushing against a stop. This is the SHOULDER_LIFT / servo-5 fault signature of 2026-07-28. See docs/hardware-fault-servo5.md for how to tell a dead servo from a jam and what to inspect (cable seating, connector, servo swap).
